problems.title: Recover a parabola vertex from three graph features
problems.question: The source parabola has roots 1,5 and y intercept −5. Find its vertex ordinate.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: y=a(x−1)(x−5); vertex abscissa is the midpoint of the roots.
steps: At x=0, 5a=−5, so a=−1. The vertex abscissa is 3.

problems.title: Three negative fractional powers
problems.question: Evaluate $0.0016^{-0.75}-0.04^{-0.5}+0.216^{-2/3}$.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
steps: The three powers are 125,5,25/9. The expression is 120+25/9=122 7/9.

problems.title: A repeated factor creates an isolated inequality solution
problems.question: Count integer solutions of $[(x^2-10x+21)(x-7)(x+1)]/|x-2|\le0$.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The numerator factors as (x−3)(x−7)²(x+1); denominator is positive except at excluded x=2.
steps: Away from x=7, the sign is determined by (x−3)(x+1), giving −1≤x≤3, with x=2 removed.
x=7 is a further zero and must be added. The integer roots of the inequality are −1,0,1,3,7.

problems.title: The value of an odd function at zero
problems.question: An odd real-domain function has seven zeros. Find f(0).
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
steps: Since −0=0, we have f(0)=−f(0), hence f(0)=0. The zero count is not needed for this value.

problems.title: A radical expression reduces to a quarter root
problems.question: Evaluate $[1/(\sqrt[4]a-1)-(\sqrt[4]a+1)/\sqrt a]\div[1/(a-2\sqrt[4]{a^3}+\sqrt a)]$ at a=√2.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Put t=a¹/⁴>0,t≠1; the final denominator is t⁴−2t³+t²=t²(t−1)².
steps: The bracket is 1/(t−1)−(t+1)/t²=1/[t²(t−1)]. Dividing by 1/[t²(t−1)²] leaves t−1.
At a=√2, t=2¹/⁸. The result is the eighth root of 2 minus 1.

problems.title: Minimum term of a quadratic sequence
problems.question: Find the least term of xₙ=2n²−19n+5 for positive integer n.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Complete the square around vertex n=19/4=4.75.
steps: The nearest integer index is 5, giving x₅=50−95+5=−40. The next nearest,4,gives −39, so −40 is the unique minimum.

problems.title: Invert a reciprocal linear function
problems.question: Find the inverse of y=1/(2x+1).
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Swap x,y and solve; the inverse input cannot be zero.
steps: x=1/(2y+1) gives 2y+1=1/x, hence y=(1−x)/(2x).

problems.title: A nested fifth and sixth root
problems.question: Simplify $\sqrt[5]{x^2\sqrt[6]{x^{-13}}}$.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The sixth root and negative exponent require x>0.
steps: The combined exponent is (2−13/6)/5=−1/30.

problems.title: A large power modulo seven
problems.question: Find the remainder of 11⁴³ divided by 7.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: 11≡4 mod7 and 4³≡1 mod7.
steps: 43=3×14+1, so 4⁴³ has the same remainder as 4.

problems.title: Four expressions in arithmetic progression
problems.question: For which y are y²−2y,3y+5,4y+13,2y²−y+25 consecutive arithmetic terms?
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Consecutive differences must agree.
steps: Equality of the first two differences gives y²−4y+3=0, so y=1 or 3.
Equality of the last two gives y²−3y+2=0, so y=1 or 2. The common value is y=1.
The resulting terms are −1,8,17,26 with common difference 9.

problems.title: A symmetric arithmetic-term sum
problems.question: An arithmetic progression satisfies a₅+a₁₀+a₁₂+a₁₅=50. Find S₂₀.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: aₙ=a₁+(n−1)d and S₂₀=20(a₁+19d/2).
steps: The given sum is 4a₁+38d=50, hence a₁+9.5d=12.5.
Multiply by 20 to get S₂₀=250.

problems.title: Averages equal the number of terms
problems.question: For every positive n, the mean of the first n arithmetic terms is n. Find a₁,d.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Mean=a₁+(n−1)d/2.
steps: At n=1, a₁=1. Matching the coefficient of n gives d/2=1, so d=2.
The terms 1,3,5,… have first-n sum n² and mean n, verifying the condition.

problems.title: Product of a geometric triple transformed into arithmetic terms
problems.question: Three geometric terms total 26. Adding 1,6,3 makes an arithmetic progression. Find their original product.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: For original terms u,v,w, uw=v² and u+1+w+3=2(v+6).
steps: The new relation gives u+w=2v+8. Combined with u+v+w=26, it yields v=6.
The product uvw=v³=216.

problems.title: Two dice with total eight
problems.question: Find the probability two fair independent dice total 8.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: All 36 ordered outcomes are equally likely.
steps: The favourable pairs are (2,6),(3,5),(4,4),(5,3),(6,2), five outcomes.

problems.title: Two uniform interval choices with a bounded sum
problems.question: Choose two numbers uniformly and independently in [−2,4]. Find probability their sum is less than 1.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: The sample region is a side-6 square; shift both inputs by 2.
steps: After shifting to u,v∈[0,6], the condition becomes u+v<5. This is a right triangle with legs 5, area 25/2.
Divide by square area 36 to get 25/72.

problems.title: An equilateral construction in a pentagon
problems.question: M is inside regular pentagon ABCDE and DEM is equilateral. Find AMC.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Each pentagon interior angle is 108°; AE=EM and CD=DM.
steps: AEM=CDM=108−60=48°. Thus the two isosceles triangles AEM,CDM each have base angles 66°.
Around M, subtract 66°,60°,66° from 360°. The remaining angle is 168°.

problems.title: Coordinate foot of an internal angle bisector
problems.question: A=(1,−5),B=(0,−2),C=(3,7). B’s internal bisector meets AC at D. Find D.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.

problems.title: A side vector from two diagonal pieces
problems.question: Diagonals of ABCD meet at O with AO:OC=1:2,BO:OD=4:3. Given OA=a,OB=b, find CD.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Opposite rays give OC=−2a and OD=−3b/4.
steps: CD=OD−OC=−3b/4+2a.

problems.title: Recover an angle from a dot-product equation
problems.question: (m+3n)·(m−n)=23, |m|=5,|n|=2. Find their angle.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Expand: |m|²+2m·n−3|n|²=23.
steps: 25+2m·n−12=23 gives m·n=5. Thus cos theta=5/(5×2)=1/2.
The angle between vectors is 60°.

problems.title: Trapezoid area from diagonal lengths and a midpoint segment
problems.question: A trapezoid’s diagonals are 3 and 5. The segment joining its base midpoints is 2. Find area.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Using suitably oriented diagonal vectors u,v, the midpoint segment is (u−v)/2; trapezoid area is |u×v|/2.
steps: |u−v|²=16=9+25−2u·v, so u·v=9. Thus the diagonal-angle cosine is 9/15=3/5 and sine 4/5.

problems.title: An equilateral triangle’s three side distances
problems.question: M is inside an equilateral triangle of side 4√3. Its distances to two sides are 1,3. Find its distance to the third.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Viviani’s theorem: the three distances total the triangle altitude.
steps: The altitude is (√3/2)(4√3)=6. The remaining distance is 6−1−3=2.

problems.title: An isosceles trapezoid with a perpendicular diagonal
problems.question: Bases of an isosceles trapezoid are 25,7 cm. A diagonal is perpendicular to a leg. Find its area.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Base half-difference is 9; a diagonal’s horizontal projection is (25+7)/2=16.
steps: Use A=(0,0),D=(25,0),B=(9,h),C=(16,h). Perpendicularity AC·CD=16×9−h²=0 gives h=12.

problems.title: A right tangential trapezoid
problems.question: A right trapezoid’s incircle radius is 12 cm. The larger contact piece of the sloping leg is 16 cm. Find area.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Height=2r; the two sloping-leg tangent lengths multiply to r²; base sum equals leg sum.
steps: The other contact piece is 144/16=9, so the sloping leg is 25. The perpendicular leg is the height 24.
The base sum is 25+24=49. Area=49×24/2=588 cm².

problems.title: Two kinds of circle tangency
problems.question: A circle centred at (4,−3) touches (x−1)²+(y−1)²=4. Find its possible radius.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: Centre distance d=√(3²+4²)=5; external tangency d=R+r and internal tangency d=|R−r|.
steps: The given radius is 2. External tangency gives r=5−2=3.
Internal tangency with the new circle surrounding the old gives r=5+2=7. Both configurations are valid. Only 3 is listed.
problems.answer: 3 among the choices; all possible radii are 3 and 7.
problems.note: The source does not specify external tangency. Internal tangency gives a second, unlisted valid radius.

problems.title: Two other sides from an incircle and one contact split
problems.question: A triangle’s inradius is 4 cm. One side’s contact pieces are 6 and 8 cm. Find the sum of its other two sides.
problems.idea: Calculate from the definitions and check any missing assumptions or alternative cases.
formulas: For vertex tangent lengths x,y,z, $r^2=xyz/(x+y+z)$ from Heron’s formula.
steps: Let the remaining tangent length be z>0. Then 16=48z/(14+z), giving 224+16z=48z and z=7.
The other sides are 6+7=13 and 8+7=15, totaling 28 cm.
